content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"Blind responses agree that 'year' has no single settled symbolic meaning; the most recognizable symbolic use is a complete, divinely appointed period of time, above all the 'acceptable year of the Lord' (Jubilee-based era of salvation, favor, and release; Isa 61:1-2; Luke 4:18-19; Lev 25). Alternatives include the day-year principle (Num 14:34; Ezek 4:5-6), the 360-day prophetic year of apocalyptic chronology, divine-time equivalence (Ps 90:4; 2 Pet 3:8), and the year as a complete natural cycle ordained by God.","book_summary":"The book defines 'year' (shanah, from a root meaning to change/repeat/return) as a turning: one complete cycle of time at whatever scale the count runs. It applies this scale-flexibility concretely, claiming Jeremiah's seventy 'years' close only as seventy jubilees, and citing Psalm 90:4's thousand years as a day.","consensus_core_identification":"A complete, divinely appointed period or cycle of time — paradigmatically the Jubilee-rooted 'year of the Lord's favor' — with context-dependent prophetic scalings (day-year, prophetic year, thousand-years-as-day) as recognized alternatives.","book_core_identification":"'Year' = one complete cycle/turning of time whose scale is elastic: the same count can run at different magnitudes (years become jubilees; a thousand years passes as a day).","core_relation":"COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book drops the soteriological Jubilee-favor center the consensus leads with, elevates the 'complete cycle' sense (a listed consensus alternative) to the core, and adds a scale-shifting rule the consensus does not state in this form: a 'year' can be re-run at a larger magnitude, so Jeremiah's seventy years are reclassified as seventy jubilees rather than a literal 70-year period or the standard 70-weeks-of-years reading. This reclassifies specific prophetic cases (Jer 25 / Dan 9) that consensus treats via literal fulfillment or the day-year/weeks-of-years calculus.","material_contradiction":"None at the core: 'one complete cycle of divinely ordered time' is compatible with, and partly contained in, the consensus field (complete-cycle alternative, day-year scaling, Ps 90:4 divine-time equivalence). The specific 'seventy jubilees' claim conflicts with common readings of Daniel 9 (seventy sevens = 490 years) but this is an application-level dispute, not a replacement of the term's referent.","rationale":"Both the book and the consensus identify 'year' fundamentally as a complete cycle/appointed period of time, and both acknowledge that prophetic 'years' can be scaled (day-year principle; thousand years as a day). The book preserves this general category but materially changes precision and extension: it makes scale-elasticity the defining feature ('at whatever scale the count is running') and uses it to reinterpret Jeremiah's seventy years as seventy jubilees — a case reclassification not found in any consensus response, which treat the 70 years literally or as expanded to 70 weeks of years. This is real boundary disagreement within a shared central category, fitting REFINED rather than DIVERGENT or MATCH.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue MATCH: the book's 'complete cycle of time' is exactly Response A/C's listed alternative, and the scaling idea is just the day-year/Ps 90:4 principle already in consensus, making the 'seventy jubilees' remark mere illustrative detail. But that reading understates the entry: the claim that Jeremiah's seventy years 'close only as seventy jubilees' is a substantive reclassification of a canonical case (Dan 9:24 says seventy weeks, i.e., 490 years — ten jubilees, not seventy), and the printed citations do not themselves establish the jubilee-scale multiplier, so the disagreement is material, not verbal.","confidence":"medium"}
